verdict.rationale: Composio documents a large catalog of 1000+ apps (1,500+ toolkits per llms.txt) with search-by-task discovery through COMPOSIO_SEARCH_TOOLS and agent plugins. The CLI also lets a person inspect tool schemas. However, the documented discovery is mainly agent-driven at runtime rather than a developer browsing the catalog before wiring anything in, and it covers Composio's own toolkits rather than a registry of third-party MCP servers. Missing for 10: a documented developer-facing catalog browse/search UI or API filterable by capability before integration, discovery of external MCP servers, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can search and browse a large catalog of MCP servers and tools by capability before wiring anything into my agent

citations.quote: By default, a session has access to every toolkit in the Composio catalog. Your agent can discover and use any of them through COMPOSIO_SEARCH_TOOLS.
The agent searches by task and selects a matching tool.
A Composio session gives your agent tool discovery, account connections, and execution across 1000+ apps.
connect apps, execute tools, inspect schemas, call authenticated APIs, and debug Composio projects.
